campus: Campus of Economics and Law, Via dei Caniana 2, Bergamo
programme_name_history: The current programme is Economics and Data Analysis (EDA). The DreamApply record contains legacy links to ls-egm.unibg.it, reflecting the earlier Economics and Global Markets (EGM) programme/site identity.
admission_type: Open access with assessment of curricular requirements and adequacy of preparation. Direct admission rules apply to qualifying Italian-degree applicants; an online oral interview is required for international/foreign-qualification applicants using pre-assessment, applicants requiring a visa, applicants who only partially meet curricular requirements, and Italian-degree applicants below the stated grade threshold.
academic_requirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent suitable foreign qualification is required. Holders of an Italian bachelor's degree in L-18, L-33, former class 17, or former class 28 qualify by degree class; they are directly admitted with a final grade of at least 81/110 and otherwise undergo an interview. Holders of other Italian degree classes need at least 48 ECTS across Economics, Business and Management, Statistics, Mathematics, Law and/or Sociology; they are directly admitted with at least 81/110 and otherwise undergo an interview. For students not yet graduated, the grade criterion is met by a weighted bachelor's examination average of at least 22/30. International and foreign-qualification candidates are individually assessed and interviewed.
entry_exam_or_test: There is no competitive entrance examination. An online oral admission interview is used to assess preparation for international/foreign-qualification applicants and other candidates falling within the programme's interview rules. Interview topics may cover the basic mathematical, econometric and economic background specified on the prospective-students page. International applicants without acceptable English evidence must also take an English-language test.
interview_required: Yes for international candidates applying for a visa, candidates with a foreign academic qualification using online pre-assessment, candidates who only partially meet curricular requirements, and Italian-degree candidates whose final grade is below 81/110 (or whose weighted average while not yet graduated is below 22/30).
selection_scoring: No numerical ranking rubric is stated for this free-access programme. The committee assesses curricular suitability and preparation; for the Italian-degree route, 81/110 (or a 22/30 weighted average for candidates not yet graduated) is the threshold for direct admission without interview.
degree_completion_deadline: A candidate may pre-enrol with a proviso under the University's general master's rules if no more than three examinations, totaling no more than 24 CFU including any internship, plus the final examination remain; any internship must already have started. The bachelor's degree must be obtained by the extraordinary March/April 2027 graduation session.
application_channel: Non-EU applicants with a foreign bachelor's degree use the UniBG online pre-evaluation route through apply.unibg.it (DreamApply), followed, where applicable, by Universitaly visa pre-enrolment. EU applicants and candidates following the ordinary route use UniBG's online student services under the free-access master's timetable.
language_requirements: English at CEFR B2 or equivalent is required. For the programme-specific route, B2 can also be evidenced by at least 6 ECTS of English in the bachelor's degree, at least six months living or working in an English-speaking country, or at least six months attending a university course abroad taught in English. International applicants who do not submit acceptable English certification with pre-application are required to take an English-language test.
accepted_english_certificates: Cambridge FCE: grades B or C
Pearson Test of English General: Level 3
TIE: minimum B2 in both oral and written tests
ESB ESOL International: minimum Pass with Merit
language_waiver_conditions: A medium-of-instruction certificate issued by the registrar or international office is accepted when the completed degree was taught entirely in English; unofficial certificates and self-declarations are not accepted. Native English-speaking applicants are exempt from English certification and medium-of-instruction evidence. The EDA programme page also recognizes 6 ECTS of English, six months in an English-speaking country, or six months of university study abroad in English as B2-equivalent evidence.

application_call_round.route: 2026/27 international pre-evaluation call 1, free-access master's programmes
2026/27 international pre-evaluation call 2, free- and limited-access master's programmes

required_documents: Bachelor degree certificate, translated into English or Italian
Official academic transcript for the last three/four years, translated into English or Italian, or Diploma Supplement
EDA Major Area Form / descriptions of major-area courses, including relevant contents, themes, aims and objectives
Valid passport showing full name, photograph and signature
course_descriptions_required: Yes. The EDA Major Area Form and major-area course descriptions are required for international online pre-evaluation.
application_fee: EUR 30 pre-evaluation fee for the 2026/27 non-EU online pre-evaluation procedure.
pre_enrolment_fee: EUR 52 for each selected master's programme; non-refundable.
enrolment_deposit: EUR 156 one-time, non-refundable enrolment fee payable on arrival in Italy, as stated in the official DreamApply programme record.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://en.unibg.it/study/enrollment/costs/taxes-and-benefits — official University tuition/taxes information. The EDA DreamApply record lists a first instalment of EUR 0-400 and a second instalment of EUR 0-1,700 depending on family income.
tuition_income_linked: Yes. Tuition contributions are income-linked through ISEEU/ISEE rules; the DreamApply record explicitly states income-dependent first and second instalments.

uncertainty_notes: The programme-specific EDA page and central UniBG pages provide current 2026/27 information. The DreamApply record's ls-egm.unibg.it links are legacy links, not a separate current programme. The EUR 156 enrolment amount is taken from the official DreamApply record and should be checked against the final central 2026/27 fee notice if the University updates it. Ordinary EU deadlines and the earlier international pre-evaluation deadlines represent different application routes.
